stem: A jar contains 11 orange tokens, 6 purple tokens, and 8 white tokens. If one token is selected at random, what is the probability that it is purple?
explanation: The total number of tokens is 11 + 6 + 8 = 25. The probability of selecting a purple token is 6/25. The answer 6/19 incorrectly excludes the white tokens from the total count. The answer 8/25 gives the probability of selecting a white token rather than a purple one. The answer 11/25 gives the probability of selecting an orange token instead.

stem: A survey of 200 employees found that 84 drink coffee, 62 drink tea, and 23 drink both coffee and tea. If an employee is selected at random, what is the probability that the employee drinks coffee or tea?
explanation: Using the inclusion-exclusion principle, P(coffee or tea) = P(coffee) + P(tea) - P(both) = 84 + 62 - 23 = 123. So the probability is 123/200. The answer 146/200 adds 84 and 62 without subtracting the 23 who drink both, double-counting those employees. The answer 84/200 considers only coffee drinkers, ignoring those who drink tea. The answer 169/200 incorrectly adds all three values (84 + 62 + 23) instead of subtracting the overlap.

stem: In a class of 150 students, 57 study French, 43 study German, and 29 study both. If a student who studies French is selected at random, what is the probability that this student also studies German?
explanation: This is a conditional probability question: P(German | French) = P(French and German) / P(French) = 29/57. The answer 29/150 divides by the total number of students instead of conditioning on those who study French. The answer 29/43 divides by the number of German students, which reverses the condition to P(French | German). The answer 57/150 gives the unconditional probability of studying French, ignoring the German requirement entirely.

skill: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
stem: A random sample of 400 voters in a city found that 164 support a proposed park renovation. Which of the following is the best estimate of the proportion of all voters in the city who support the renovation?
explanation: The sample proportion is 164/400 = 0.41, which is the best estimate of the population proportion. The value 0.36 results from an arithmetic error in the division. The value 0.50 assumes an even split without using the sample data. The value 0.64 incorrectly uses (400 - 164)/400 = 236/400, giving the proportion who do not support the renovation.

skill: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
stem: A researcher surveys a random sample of 600 residents and finds that 43% favor a new transit line. The margin of error for the survey is 4 percentage points. Which of the following is a valid conclusion?

options.text: Exactly 43% of all residents favor the transit line.
Between 39% and 47% of all residents likely favor the transit line.
At most 47% of all residents favor the transit line.
Between 43% and 47% of all residents likely favor the transit line.

explanation: A margin of error of 4 percentage points means the confidence interval is 43% minus 4% to 43% plus 4%, or 39% to 47%. The claim that exactly 43% of all residents favor it treats the sample statistic as a population parameter. The claim of at most 47% only uses the upper bound and ignores the full interval. The range 43% to 47% only adds the margin of error in one direction, omitting the lower bound of 39%.

skill: Inference from Sample Statistics and Margin of Error
stem: Two independent random samples are taken from the same population. Sample A has 250 respondents and finds that 58% agree with a policy. Sample B has 1,000 respondents and finds that 54% agree. Which of the following best explains the difference in results?

options.text: Sample B is more likely to be biased because it is larger.
The difference is most likely due to sampling variability, and Sample B's estimate is expected to have a smaller margin of error.
Sample A's result should be preferred because it found a higher percentage.
Neither result can be trusted because the two samples disagree.

explanation: Random samples from the same population can produce different statistics due to sampling variability. Larger samples have smaller margins of error, so the 1,000-respondent estimate is expected to be more precise. The claim that a larger sample is more biased reverses the relationship between sample size and reliability. Preferring a result simply because it yielded a higher percentage has no statistical basis. Dismissing both results because they differ ignores the expected variability inherent in random sampling.

skill: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
stem: A researcher wants to determine whether a new fertilizer increases tomato yield. She randomly assigns 30 tomato plants to receive the new fertilizer and 30 plants to receive a standard fertilizer. This study is best described as which of the following?

options.text: An observational study
A survey
An experiment
A census

explanation: Because the researcher randomly assigns treatments (new fertilizer vs. standard fertilizer) to subjects, this is an experiment. An observational study would observe plants without assigning treatments. A survey collects self-reported data from respondents, which does not apply to measuring plant yield. A census collects data from every member of a population, whereas this study uses a sample of 60 plants.

skill: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
stem: A hospital reviews medical records and finds that patients who exercised at least 3 times per week had lower rates of heart disease than patients who exercised less frequently. Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?

options.text: Exercising at least 3 times per week causes a reduction in heart disease.
There is an association between exercising at least 3 times per week and lower rates of heart disease.
Patients who exercise less frequently should be required to exercise more.
The hospital should recommend exercise only to patients with heart disease.

explanation: Since this is an observational study (reviewing existing records without random assignment), only an association can be established, not causation. The causal claim that exercise causes a reduction in heart disease is not supported because confounding variables were not controlled through random assignment. The recommendation to require exercise goes beyond what the data supports and introduces a policy judgment. Recommending exercise only to patients with heart disease misinterprets the finding, which compares exercise frequency across all patients.

skill: Evaluating Statistical Claims: Observational Studies and Experiments
stem: Researchers want to test whether a new study technique improves exam scores. They recruit 80 volunteers and let each volunteer choose whether to use the new technique or their usual method. Students using the new technique score an average of 7 points higher. A critic argues the study has a flaw. Which of the following best describes the flaw?

options.text: The sample size of 80 is too small to detect a 7-point difference.
The study lacks a control group because all participants took the exam.
Self-selection into groups means differences in scores could be due to pre-existing differences between the groups rather than the technique.
The 7-point difference is not statistically significant because it is less than 10 points.

explanation: When participants self-select into treatment and control groups, confounding variables undermine causal conclusions. Students who chose the new technique may already be more motivated or higher-performing, so the 7-point difference could reflect pre-existing differences rather than the technique itself. The claim about sample size is incorrect because 80 participants can be sufficient to detect a meaningful effect. The study does have a comparison group (those using their usual method), so the claim that it lacks a control group is wrong. Statistical significance depends on variability and sample size, not on an arbitrary threshold of 10 points.
